messages:
Maria Chen: Quick design scrub — dropped two updated mockups for the Settings form validation patterns. Mock 1: field-first errors (inline message + red outline). Mock 2: subtle inline hints + top summary with expandable details. Also sketched bulk-delete confirmation variations. Looking for accessibility, copy clarity, and mobile density feedback. Devin Patel: skimmed both. My read: inline-first feels immediate for single edits, summary is better for long multi-section forms. Concern: top toast might hide on smaller screens and be easy to miss. Samir K.: +1. Inline-only becomes noisy in dense grant/admin tables. For bulk operations we likely need hybrid: per-row inline markers and a collapsible summary when failures exceed 3 rows. Rika Sato: A11y note: if we keep a top summary it must be announced via aria-live and focus should move to it after a failed submit. Example pattern suggestion: ```
Save failed: 3 items require attention. Expand for details.
``` Maria Chen: Good. Draft copy for the summary: "Save failed — 3 problems need attention. Review the list or fix fields inline." Is this too wordy? Devin Patel: Trim for scannability: "Save failed — 3 issues. See details below." Also, programmatically focus the first invalid field after the summary is announced for keyboard users. Samir K.: Required marker discussion: current comps use an asterisk only. Evidence suggests asterisk alone isn't always discoverable. Options: keep asterisk + visible "Required" helper or rely on aria-required + tooltip. I lean toward explicit "Required" text on dense admin forms. Rika Sato: Agree — show the word "Required" for critical inputs. Keep `aria-required` too. On narrow breakpoints we can collapse the visual label to an asterisk but keep `aria-label`/`aria-required` intact. Maria Chen: Proposed helper copy example: label: "Organization name" helper: "Required — used for billing and public URLs." Short, actionable. Devin Patel: Bulk destructive confirmation ideas: 1) modal with typed-confirm (type DELETE), 2) modal requiring exact-name typing, 3) non-blocking snackbar with undo. For irreversible org-level deletes prefer typed-confirm or exact-name. For reversible/soft deletes prefer snackbar undo. Samir K.: Typed-confirm good for safety but slows admins. Maybe: exact-name for org-level, typed-confirm for dataset/table-level irreversible deletes, snackbar undo for daily bulk ops. Add an explicit countdown before finalizing if it's a long-running operation. Rika Sato: Accessibility for typing confirmations: ensure the input has proper label and instructions announced. Provide a no-mouse keyboard flow and confirm buttons reachable via keyboard. Also ensure high-contrast focus styles for that input. Maria Chen: DesignBot quick run: flagged two things — inline helper contrast too low, and the summary lacked explicit focus transfer. DesignBot: Accessibility scan: helper text contrast ratio 3.6:1 (fail). Recommend >= 4.5:1 or stronger weight. `aria-live` region in Mock 2 missing `aria-label`; recommend `aria-label="Form errors"` and set focus to the region after submit failure. Also recommend adding `aria-invalid` on invalid inputs. Devin Patel: Actionable list: 1) bump inline helper contrast >= 4.5:1 or increase weight; 2) implement focus transfer to the summary on submit failure and focus first invalid field; 3) prefer explicit "Required" label for dense/admin forms (asterisk optional); 4) adopt exact-name/typed-confirm patterns only for irreversible deletes; use snackbar undo for soft bulk-deletes. Maria Chen: Nice. I'll open a small PR with copy + a11y fixes and post updated mocks. Tagging @Samir to own exact-name copy candidates for the org-delete modal. Thanks all :slightly_smiling_face:
